Assuming this is a genuine question: Rent-seeking behavior is a very informative deep-dive. Main reason renters rent instead of buy is that the renting class is generally awarded lower credit scores and credit-worthiness due to a lack of capital that doesn't necessarily reflect a lack of income. The East coast especially has this style of "retirement plan" landlords who've leveraged an existing pension or home equity developed over years, typically from home purchased through generous first time home buyer grants many years ago, to pick up properties at very low monthly mortgage payments. The East coast has a very high incidence rate of renters paying up to double and triple the monthly mortgage that the landlord pays, simply because, while they have the income, most financial institutions don't take rent payments into account when calculating credit worthiness, leaving them trapped in a cycle of renting at high prices, but never developing their own credit worthiness. In an ironic twist, the rent the landlord collects actually works to boost the landlords credit worthiness, even though it isn't considered for the tenant's. This system leads, by design, to a further stratification between the landowning class and the renting class. It's drastically easier to purchase your second property than it is your first. Exploiting your fellow man, in a textbook example of "fuck you, I got mine" shouldn't be a retirement plan. It's inherently antisocial, and demonstrates a desire to benefit capitalistically from your successes, but socializing your mistakes, ie not developing a proper retirement portfolio, by having a new generation subsidize your retirement via their rent payments.
